HoneyFactory external API. All `/api` endpoints except `/api/login` and `/api/health` require a token in the request header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**Tokens**: Use a session token obtained at login (valid for 7 days), or a token starting with `vf_` created on the "API Tokens" page. API tokens support
scopes (read: read-only / write: read + write tags / control: read/write + simulation control, fault injection, test scripts / admin: same permissions as the creator), factory restrictions, expiration dates, and IP allowlists.

**Common workflow**

1. `GET /api/plants` lists factories; `GET /api/p/{pid}/points/v2` retrieves the structured tag list (OPC UA NodeIds, MQTT topics, Modbus addresses).
2. `POST /api/p/{pid}/station/{sid}/write` writes a setpoint: `{"tag": "Setpoint/TapTemp", "value": 1500}`.
3. `POST /api/p/{pid}/signals/comm` injects a communication fault: `{"protocol": "mqtt", "mode": "drop", "station": "CNC1", "drop_pct": 30, "minutes": 5}`.
4. `POST /api/p/{pid}/tests/run` runs a test script; `GET /api/p/{pid}/tests/runs/{rid}/junit.xml` retrieves the JUnit report.

**Protocol connectivity essentials**

- OPC UA: `opc.tcp://<host>:4840/vfactory/`, namespace `http://honeymeta.cn/vfactory`, NodeId `ns=2;s=<factory>/<equipment>/<tag>`.
  Numeric tags use AnalogItemType (with EngineeringUnits and EURange), support SourceTimestamp and HistoryRead (24 hours), and emit alarms as AlarmConditionType events.
  Out-of-range writes return BadOutOfRange.
- MQTT: Topic `vfactory/<factory>/<area>/<equipment>/<tag>`, payload `{"value", "unit", "quality", "ts", "sim_ts", "wall_ts"}`;
  send writes to `…/set` (`{"value": x, "id": "request ID"}` or a plain number). Acknowledgments appear on `…/set/ack`; failures are also published to `vfactory/<factory>/_errors`.
- Modbus TCP: One port per factory, one Unit per device; see the tag list for full addresses. Exception codes: 02 address out of range/read-only, 03 value out of range, 04 slave failure, 0B slave not found.

Switch the external time source (simulation clock or wall clock) in "Protocol Settings" under Signals.

## Files
- tags.csv: Wide-format time series. Column names use Equipment/Tag format, such as CNC1/Monitoring/Spindle/Load. Empty values indicate that the equipment did not exist at that time.
- events.csv: Production log (heats, tool changes, alarms, failures, repairs, plans, scenario actions, etc.). The data column contains structured JSON fields.
- parts.csv: Part records. truth_defects contains actual defects from the simulation (ground truth); inspection_* contains inspection station results and can be used to evaluate missed defects and misclassifications.
- labels.csv: Labeled intervals. type values: failure for equipment failure, fault for injected anomalies (such as tool breakage or moisture sensor drift), planned for scheduled downtime/non-production time,
  changeover for changeovers, scenario for scenario actions, and comm for communication failures. An end value of "In Progress" means the interval was still ongoing at export time.

## Usage
- Anomaly detection: Train on tags.csv and evaluate against failure/fault intervals in labels.csv.
- Quality prediction: Use pouring parameters in parts.csv (pour_temp, mg, sand_moisture, compactability, ce) to predict truth_defects.
- Tool wear: Use CNCx/Monitoring/Spindle/Load and Tools/Txx/LifeCount with tool change events in events.csv.
